evidence: COLREG.2/Circ.20 (5 August 1983, MSC 48) in https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526: new scheme .2 'In the approaches to Galveston Bay', 'will not be implemented before 17 December 1983' confirmed. eCFR 167.350 coordinates confirmed (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=167). Table 161.12(c) row (3) Houston-Galveston quote present verbatim (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=161): every TSS point (southernmost 29°06.40'N, easternmost 94°20.60'W) lies inside the box. 161.35(a) VTS area includes Galveston Bay Entrance Channel and Outer Bar Channel; Table 161.35(c) reporting point 1 LB '1C' 29°18.2'N 94°37.6'W; own point-in-polygon test confirms it lies inside the inshore precautionary area (167.350(a)). NAVCEN: operating area 'includes the Houston Ship Channel from the sea buoy ...' (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/vessel-traffic-services-locations). Note 4 caveat about monitoring areas beyond navigable waters present verbatim; the offshore precautionary area is well offshore so the researcher's caveat is appropriate. 33 CFR 169 has no Gulf system.

eCFR 167.150-155 (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=167): 7-mile radius precautionary area centred 40°27.50'N 73°49.90'W. 161.25 and Table 161.12(c) row (7) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=161): VTS New York area's southern limit is 'a line connecting the entrance buoys at the Ambrose Channel, Swash Channel, and Sandy Hook Channel to Sandy Hook Point'. The researcher left the precautionary-area overlap 'not verified'. Own check: USCG Local Notice to Mariners (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/lnms/lnm01052026.pdf) gives the eastern end of the Ambrose Federal Navigation Channel at about 40°28'38"N 073°53'41"W to 40°28'56"N 073°53'30"W, which is about 3.1 nm from the precautionary area centre, well inside the 7-mile radius. The circle reaches about 73°59'W, so the outer Ambrose Channel and the Lower Bay waters north of the entrance-buoy line (VTS New York area) overlap the landward part of the scheme's precautionary area. The precautionary area is a component of the Off New York TSS (167.150-151), so the VTS covers part of the scheme and the direct approach to the lanes. The researcher is right that the lanes themselves lie outside. Identity: Circ.20 lists .12 'Off New York' as amended; Circ.5 lists 'Off New York' for 15 May 1978 implementation. Reporting: WHALESNORTH south limit 41°00'N and WHALESSOUTH 30°00'N-31°27'N (33 CFR 169.105/169.115, https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=169) confirmed; scheme lies 39°45'N-40°37'N, outside both.
recommended_change: VTS: change 'Unresolved' to 'Confirmed present' (VTS New York), partial: 'Landward part of the 7 NM circular precautionary area (33 CFR 167.151(a)) overlaps the VTS New York area north of the Ambrose/Swash/Sandy Hook entrance-buoy line (33 CFR 161.25; Table 161.12(c)); Ambrose Channel eastern end about 3 NM from the precautionary area centre (USCG LNM 05/2026). Traffic lanes and outer precautionary area are outside the VTS area.'

evidence: eCFR 167.100-103 (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=167) confirmed (two precautionary areas, two approaches; USCG-2010-0718). Circ.20 .13 amended scheme confirmed (https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526). No VTS in 33 CFR 161 Subpart C or Table 161.12(c) and none on NAVCEN list of 12 (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/vessel-traffic-services-locations); Unresolved rather than absent is correct. Reporting: Table 161.12(c) row (2) Buzzards Bay VMRS boundary quote verified (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-33.xml?part=161). Own geometry: Buzzards Bay approach separation-zone end (41°21.80'N 71°07.10'W) is 3.1 nm from the Sakonnet Point-Buzzards Bay Entrance Light-Cuttyhunk line; lane outer corners are 2.9 and 3.4 nm from it. The northern Narragansett precautionary area (radius 3.55 nm on 41°25.60'N 71°23.30'W) lies well west of Sakonnet Point (71°11.7'W). So no part of the TSS lies in VMRS Buzzards Bay. The researcher's own text says the VMRS 'applies in the waters the lane leads into, not in the TSS'. The rule requires coverage of the scheme, part of it, or its direct approach; the TSS is the approach to the VMRS, not the reverse. 'Confirmed present' is therefore too strong. WHALESNORTH western limit (69°17'W to 70°02'W) confirmed well east.
recommended_change: Reporting: change 'Confirmed present' to 'Unresolved' with note: 'VMRS Buzzards Bay (33 CFR 161, Table 161.12(c) row 2) begins about 3 NM north of the landward end of the Buzzards Bay approach; no mandatory reporting system covers the TSS itself.' Correct '3.5 NM' to 'about 3 NM'.

evidence: Circ.20-era note in https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526: 'In the Bay of Fundy and approaches' not effective before 1 June 1983; COLREG.2/Circ.52 annex 5 amended scheme 'consists of two parts', implemented 0000 UTC 1 July 2003: confirmed. Transportstyrelsen 2017 list also includes it. SOR/2025-275 (registered 2025-12-12) verified: s.3(1)(a) quote present; Schedule 3 item 7 Bay of Fundy boundary runs through 44°09'30.3"N 66°47'01"W, 44°11'50.3"N 66°49'31"W and 44°14'57.3"N 66°52'40"W, which coincide with the TSS Part I south-west end points (44°11.83'N 66°49.55'W; 44°14.95'N 66°52.70'W in Circ.52), so the zone boundary is drawn along the TSS entrance. RAMN 2026 PDF Table 3-24 lists calling-in point 1A 'Southwest entrance to traffic separation scheme Inward A point at 44°10'40.3"N 066°48'16"W' (the record cites Tables 3-28 to 3-30 of the web version; numbering differs). s.39 repeals SOR/89-98 and SOR/89-99 confirmed. Reporting: sections 10-11 and Part 4 are sailing plan, position, final and deviation reports owed to the VTS (Fundy Traffic) under the VTS Zones Regulations. Under the register rule this is routine VTS reporting, not a separate mandatory reporting scheme, and the same researcher treated the same Regulations that way in TSS-0131. No IMO-adopted SOLAS V/11 system for the Bay of Fundy was evidenced.
recommended_change: Reporting: change 'Confirmed present' to 'Unresolved' with note: 'Sailing plan, position and final reports under SOR/2025-275 (Local Eastern VTS Zone, Fundy Traffic) are VTS participation duties recorded with the service; no separate mandatory ship reporting system found.' evidence: https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526: COLREG.2/Circ.5 (6 March 1978) lists '9. In the Approaches to Valparaiso' for implementation on 15 May 1978; COLREG.2/Circ.32 (MSC 55) amended scheme implemented 0000 UTC 15 October 1988, with coordinates (separation zone 32°57.62'S 71°37.27'W to 33°00.53'S 71°36.52'W). The passage actually quoted for this source (Peru schemes, Circ.48) does not mention Valparaíso. Transportstyrelsen routeing list dated 2017-04-27 (https://transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/ruttsystem.pdf) still lists it, so 'Provisional' pending a current SHOA/GISIS check is fair. CHILREP PDF (https://www.directemar.cl/directemar/site/docs/20200515/20200515201601/chilrep_v2_espa__ol.pdf) quotes present: 'El CHILREP es un sistema voluntario' and 'Los buques de bandera chilena deben notificar su posición a las 12:00Z y 24:00Z diariamente'. Nuance: the same page also says foreign ships navigating Chilean internal waters ('aguas interiores') must report position at 12:00Z and 24:00Z; this does not evidently apply to an approach TSS in the territorial sea. vLex not re-opened (secondary source; researcher correctly did not rely on it). False-negative search (1 web action): found only a mundomaritimo.cl news item on the Valparaíso VTS-AIS control tower (not official, no service area); no easy official DIRECTEMAR source.
recommended_change: Cite COLREG.2/Circ.5 and Circ.32 annex item 10 as the identity passages (not the Circ.48 Peru text). Reporting note: add that CHILREP requires position reports from foreign ships only in Chilean internal waters. No verdict change.

evidence: Transportstyrelsen list (https://transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/ruttsystem.pdf) entry 'In the approaches to Ijmuiden Colreg.2/Circ.64 2012 MSC 91 2012' present. The Circ.64 text the researcher did not retrieve is in https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526: MSC 91 (26-30 November 2012) adopted 'In the approaches to IJmuiden' (new scheme), implemented 0000 UTC 1 August 2013, comprising IJmuiden West Inner TSS (east ends 52°29.47'N 4°20.03'E, 52°28.70'N 4°19.80'E; lanes to 52°30.52'N 4°20.35'E and 52°27.62'N 4°19.48'E), IJmuiden North TSS and IJmuiden West Outer TSS (to about 3°55'E). Port of Amsterdam VTS directive (https://www.portofamsterdam.com/sites/default/files/2025-09/2025-479_VTS%20communicatieregeling%202.0%20def_NLEN_rev.pdf) scope (a) quote present verbatim (Territorial Sea within 12 nm radius of the seaward ends of the IJmuiden breakwaters, including the extended IJ-geul). Own geometry, using an approximate breakwater-head position of 52°28.0'N 4°32.3'E (not from an official source): the West Inner TSS east end points are about 7.6 to 7.8 nm away and its points near 4°12'E about 12.2 to 12.7 nm, so roughly the eastern 4 to 5 nm of the West Inner TSS lies within the VTS area; the North and West Outer TSS (about 14.7 nm and beyond) lie outside. The 4 nm margin is far larger than any plausible error in the breakwater position. The Inner TSS lanes flank the IJ-geul, which the directive expressly includes. Reporting: section 8 duties to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 are VTS reporting; no IMO or national SRS found.
recommended_change: VTS: change 'Unresolved' to 'Confirmed present' (VTS North Sea Canal Area, IJmuiden Approaches), partial: 'Eastern part of the IJmuiden West Inner TSS (about 4°12'E to 4°20'E, COLREG.2/Circ.64 annex 1) lies within the 12 NM radius of the IJmuiden breakwater heads defined in the Port of Amsterdam VTS directive; IJmuiden North and West Outer TSS lie outside.' Confirm the breakwater-head coordinates from Netherlands chart 1631 or a Port of Amsterdam source. Identity: replace 'Circ.64 text not retrieved' with the Circ.64 annex 1 citation.
